As someone closer to 40 than 30 I tend to think of some anime that's targeted towards kids as being targeted to parents too.

One that springs to mind is Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi. It has plenty of shit for kids, with a new world in every episode and plenty of adventure, but it also has an overarching plot covering the pain of growing up, and a ton of references to older styles and genres of anime that some folks grew up with.

I know that it's not cool to state the obvious and that your anime cred is directly related to how esoteric your recommendation is, but just in case any non-anime folks read this thread...

Studio Ghibli is the Pixar of the anime world. Just like how many adults will enjoy Lassiter's movies, Miyazaki is awesome for all ages.

If you haven't seen them yet, Disney just released a bunch of them with good English dubs last year. I started my wife (38) on Ponyo, Kiki, and Totoro. Now she's seen about 8 movies and asks when we can see more.
I typically try to find their interests and tailor the anime to them. Shinichiro Watanabe shows are a safe go to imo.
I think Usagi Drop would fit under this. I think it's considered Josei but I think it resonates most with fathers. I love it.

Seinen and Josei are the categories for things aimed at older viewers. So you should browse series in those categories for something the person in question might like.

Monster is a good series about an up and coming Japanese doctor living in Germany who after choosing to save a child's life is surrounded by murders with him as the prime suspect. It follows his life after being ruined and trying to figure out the truth.
